title: One home for the keys?
hook: Which search needs fewer possible box checks?

knows: Everyday objects have sizes, positions and amounts
doesNotKnow: that if the keys always go back to one place, finding them takes one check, while an unknown place can mean checking every spot

misconception: A 'usual place' for keys helps only a little, because you still end up looking around.
objective: In the stated worst-case search, an unknown location may require checking every box. A maintained address directs the search to one box; the benefit depends on returning the item to that address.

recall.question: Your keys have a fixed bowl among 6 possible places. What keeps the worst-case search at 1 check?
options: A bowl placed right next to the front door
A bright tag on the key ring
Returning them to the bowl every time
recall.why: An address cuts the worst case from 6 checks to 1 only if the keys go back to it. Leave them elsewhere once and the search can be all 6 places again.
